summary:
COSMOS is an interactive, browser-based space exploration game designed to introduce children aged 7–12 to the challenges of managing a lunar outpost. Players step into the role of junior astronauts, build their mission identity, explore a 3D space environment, and complete interactive missions that introduce the decisions involved in real space exploration.

The experience combines space-themed storytelling, interactive gameplay, mission challenges, and immersive 3D environments to make STEM learning engaging and accessible. Players encounter mission scenarios that encourage logical thinking, problem-solving, and an understanding of how astronauts navigate unfamiliar environments and operational constraints. By transforming space exploration concepts into hands-on activities rather than passive lessons, COSMOS aims to make scientific learning more memorable and enjoyable.

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of explorers by making them feel like active participants in a space mission while building curiosity about the Moon, space technology, and human exploration beyond Earth.
details:
COSMOS is an interactive, browser-based space mission training experience that puts children aged 7–12 in the role of junior astronauts. Players embark on a space expedition, explore immersive 3D environments, travel between destinations such as the Moon and Mars, and progress through a structured 30-mission journey.

How it works: The experience combines an interactive astronaut character, 3D exploration environments, mission-control interactions, and short, age-appropriate mission activities. Players encounter different scenarios as their expedition progresses, including spacecraft preparation, destination exploration, and surface-level tasks. The mission system follows a structured progression, with destination-specific activities and branching possibilities that introduce children to the complexity of space exploration.

Technology: We developed the application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, with Python and FastAPI powering the backend and mission-related APIs. We also incorporated NASA-related mission datasets and an OSDR (Open Science Data Repository) crosswalk to support scientific context and data-informed educational content. AI-assisted mission generation is supported through a structured API design, with a curated mission catalogue as a fallback. The project is designed to run in a web browser without requiring dedicated hardware.

Creativity and impact: Rather than teaching astronomy through static information or conventional quizzes, COSMOS uses exploration, storytelling, interactive challenges, and game mechanics to make children active participants in a simulated space expedition. It aims to develop curiosity, logical reasoning, problem-solving, and an appreciation of the decisions involved in human spaceflight.

Design considerations: Our team prioritised child-friendly language, accessible interactions, short missions, intuitive navigation, engaging 3D environments, and a balance between scientific authenticity and entertainment. Our ultimate goal is to make complex space exploration concepts approachable and inspire children to see themselves as future scientists, engineers, and astronauts.
